name: priest
lore:
Priests, as described in Dungeons & Dragons lore, are not a distinct class but rather a role often embodied by clerics. These individuals serve as intermediaries between the mortal realm and the divine, acting as conduits for the power of their chosen deity. They are devoted followers, driven by unwavering faith and a desire to spread the teachings and influence of their god or pantheon. Their lives are typically dedicated to prayer, service, and the performance of sacred rites, all in the name of their divine patron.

Clerics, fulfilling the priest role, are granted divine abilities as a reward for their devotion. These powers can manifest in various ways, from healing the wounded and bolstering allies to smiting enemies and manipulating the very fabric of reality. The specific powers available to a cleric are often tied to the domains or aspects of their deity, reflecting the god's unique portfolio and influence. Whether cloistered in temples, wandering as missionaries, or leading armies in holy wars, priests (clerics) are a potent force in any D&D world.

Because 'priest' directs to 'cleric' in D&D settings, understanding the class features and role-playing guides associated with clerics provides the best insight into the typical depiction of a priest. Their connection to the divine, their unwavering faith, and the potent magic they wield make them pivotal figures in the ongoing struggle between good and evil, order and chaos, that shapes the D&D multiverse.
